en.name: White fungus (snow fungus)
en.summary: Dried white fungus keeps 6–12 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard — a general figure for dried vegetables rather than one published for fungus. Once it is soaked there is no timeline at all, only a rule: soak no more than two hours at room temperature, refrigerate the bowl if it needs longer, and use it at once.
en.pantry: Keep it in a sealed jar in a cool, dry, dark cupboard, and take 6–12 months as a working range. Be clear about where that comes from: it is the general shelf life given for dried vegetables, where one source allows roughly half a year in a cool room and only a few months in a warm one, and another gives a full year at ordinary room temperature. Nothing specific to snow fungus has been published. The brittle fans crumble easily and the crumbs then absorb damp fastest, so a rigid jar beats a bag, and the desiccant sachet is worth keeping.
en.fridge: There is no refrigerated shelf life for soaked white fungus, and that is the honest answer rather than a gap — what exists is a handling rule, and it is the important part of this record. Soaking at room temperature should take no more than two hours; if it needs longer than that, put the soaking bowl in the refrigerator instead of leaving it on the counter. Use the soaked fungus as soon as possible, and discard it if it turns slimy or smells abnormal. Dried fungus itself can be kept sealed in the fridge in a humid kitchen, which protects it from damp, but it is the soaking step that carries the risk.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for white fungus, dried or soaked. Freezing the dried fans achieves little — they already keep for months sealed, and their problem is moisture rather than time — and freezing soaked fungus wrecks the crunch that is the whole point of it in a dessert soup. A cooked 銀耳湯 does freeze in portions if you want to keep it, and it should be cooled quickly before it goes in.
spoilage: Musty smell, damp softness or visible mould on the dried fans.
Soaked fungus that has turned slimy or slippery.
Any abnormal, sour or fermented smell after soaking.
Dark patches or unusual yellowing on a fungus that should be pale cream.
tips: Store in a rigid airtight jar; the fans crumble and the crumbs soak up damp.
Soak in plenty of cold water and no longer than two hours at room temperature.
Put the soaking bowl in the fridge if it needs longer, and use the fungus straight away.
Trim the hard yellow base before cooking.

faq.q: How long does dried white fungus keep?
faq.a: 6–12 months sealed in a cool dark cupboard. That is the general figure for dried vegetables, not one published for snow fungus.

faq.q: How long can white fungus soak?
faq.a: No more than two hours at room temperature. If it needs longer, refrigerate the soaking bowl, and use the fungus as soon as it is ready.

faq.q: Can you keep soaked white fungus?
faq.a: There is no published timeline for it. Use it as soon as possible, and discard it if it turns slimy or smells abnormal.

zh.name: 白木耳
zh.summary: 乾燥白木耳密封放陰涼避光的櫥櫃約 6～12 個月——這是乾燥蔬菜的通則數字，不是為白木耳公布的。泡發之後則完全沒有期限可言，只有一條規則：室溫泡發不超過兩小時，需要更久就把整碗放冰箱，泡好盡快使用。
zh.pantry: 密封罐放陰涼、乾燥、避光的櫥櫃，6～12 個月當作工作範圍。這個數字的來歷要講清楚：它是乾燥蔬菜的一般保存期限，其中一份資料在涼爽室溫下給約半年、在溫暖環境只給幾個月，另一份則在一般室溫下給整整一年。針對白木耳本身，沒有任何公布的數據。乾燥的木耳很脆、容易碎，而碎屑吸濕最快，所以硬殼密封罐比塑膠袋好，乾燥劑也值得留著。
zh.fridge: 泡發後的白木耳沒有冷藏保存期限，而這是誠實的答案而不是資料缺漏——存在的是一條處理規則，而它才是這一則真正的重點。室溫泡發不應超過兩小時；需要更久的話，請把泡的碗放進冰箱，不要留在流理台上。泡好要盡快使用，一旦變得黏滑或聞起來不對，就丟掉。乾木耳本身在潮濕的廚房可以密封冰起來防潮，但真正有風險的環節是泡發。
zh.freezer: 不論乾的還是泡開的白木耳，都沒有公布的冷凍期限。把乾木耳冷凍幫助有限——它密封就能放好幾個月，問題出在水分而不是時間；把泡開的冷凍則會毀掉它在甜湯裡最重要的脆度。煮好的銀耳湯倒是可以分小份冷凍，下冷凍前要先快速降溫。
spoilage: 乾木耳有霉味、摸起來受潮發軟，或看得到霉。
泡發後出現任何異常的酸味或發酵味。
本該是淡奶油色的木耳出現深色斑或不正常的黃化。
tips: 用硬殼氣密罐保存，木耳易碎、碎屑最會吸濕。
用大量冷水泡，室溫下不要超過兩小時。
需要泡更久就把碗放冰箱，泡好立刻使用。
烹調前把底部黃黃硬硬的蒂頭剪掉。

faq.a: 密封放陰涼暗處約 6～12 個月。這是乾燥蔬菜的通則數字，不是白木耳專屬的公布資料。
室溫下不要超過兩小時。需要更久就把泡的碗放冰箱，而且泡好要立刻使用。

faq.q: 泡開的白木耳可以放嗎？
faq.a: 沒有公布的期限。請盡快使用，一旦變黏滑或聞起來不對就丟掉。
